- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:658-679 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  File: scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 658-679 (first deterministic fallback, when DIAGNOSE_SUCCESS != true)
  Problem: The deterministic fallback JSON generated when Codex diagnose fails omits the `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis` top-level fields. The judge-fix commit instructions at entry[15] explicitly stated: "Leave the prompt/static-prefix wording, rendered-prompt contract coverage, `format_diagnose_trace_section`, and the deterministic fallback payload/body fields intact; those are compatible with the prompt/contract work and do not need rollback." The commit removed them anyway, and also removed `format_diagnose_trace_section` entirely. The diagnose contract in `prompts/mode-implement-diagnose.txt:82-86` declares `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis` as required top-level fields when `DIAGNOSE_TRACE_REQUIRED=true`, and `prompts/contracts/mode-implement-diagnose.yml` sets that default to `true`. The fallback JSON diverging from this contract means downstream consumers of `IMPLEMENT_DIAGNOSE_RESULT_FILE` see a different JSON shape depending on whether Codex succeeded or fell back.
  Why it fails at runtime: Any tooling or script that reads `IMPLEMENT_DIAGNOSE_RESULT_FILE` and expects `evidence_trace`/`hypothesis` (per the documented contract) will find them absent in failure-mode runs. The fallback fix-up issue body also lost the trace context that helps downstream implement runs understand what went wrong.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:690-708 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  File: scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 690-708 (empty fix_issues fallback)
  Problem: The empty `fix_issues` fallback JSON omits `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis`, and the fallback issue body no longer carries the trace section that was previously formatted from the diagnose output. Before the judge-fix commit, this path extracted `EXISTING_EVIDENCE_TRACE_JSON`, `EXISTING_HYPOTHESIS`, and called `format_diagnose_trace_section` to preserve diagnostic context in the generated fix-up issue. After the commit, the fallback body is a bare "No fix_issues were returned" message with no trace or hypothesis context.
  Why it fails at runtime: When diagnose returns `needs_fixes` with a valid trace/hypothesis but an empty `fix_issues` array, the generated fix-up issue body loses the diagnostic evidence that would help the downstream implement run understand what was found. The downstream implementer only sees "No fix_issues were returned" without the trace that was already computed.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
